title: Lung Cancer Management
specialty: Thoracic Oncology, Respiratory Medicine and Thoracic Surgery

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with suspected or confirmed lung cancer: urgent referral and chest X-ray criteria, CT/PET staging, tissue and molecular testing, MDT treatment by stage, and follow-up. Verified against the Saudi lung cancer management guidelines (2017), NICE NG122 and NICE NG12, with lung screening eligibility from the Saudi PHA 2023 guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi guideline 2017 predates newer immunotherapy and targeted agents

pathophysiology.summary: Lung cancer arises from bronchial epithelium, most often after tobacco exposure. It is divided into non-small-cell (adenocarcinoma, squamous) and small-cell carcinoma. Driver mutations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1) and PD-L1 expression guide systemic therapy in NSCLC.
keyMechanisms: Carcinogens in smoke cause cumulative DNA damage.
Adenocarcinoma in never-smokers often carries EGFR or ALK alterations, treatable with tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
Small-cell carcinoma grows fast and spreads early.

symptoms: Cough, haemoptysis, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, appetite loss, fatigue (NICE NG12 1.1.2).
Hoarseness, superior vena cava obstruction, bone pain.
physicalSigns: Clubbing, lymphadenopathy, effusion, signs of SVC obstruction.
redFlags: Unexplained haemoptysis at 40 or over — suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12 1.1.1)
Neurological signs — brain metastases or cord compression

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Common in KSA; sputum AFB and culture.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: Urgent chest X-ray or suspected cancer referral per NICE NG12 1.1.1–1.1.3.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose and stage
actions: CT before biopsy (NICE 1.2.14); PET-CT if curative treatment possible (NICE 1.2.4).
EBUS-TBNA for nodes 10 mm or more when nodal stage affects treatment (NICE 1.2.8, 1.2.17).
Discuss all new cases at tumour board; fitness tests (PFT, ECG, echo) before surgery (SLCG 1.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage I–II NSCLC
actions: Anatomical resection with lymph node sampling (SLCG 2.1–2.4).
Adjuvant platinum doublet (4–6 cycles, cisplatin preferred) for stage IB high-risk and II (SLCG 2.2.3, 2.3.2).
Inoperable: SBRT with curative intent; poor PFTs are not a contraindication (SLCG 2.3.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage III NSCLC
actions: N2 disease: concurrent chemoradiotherapy is standard; surgery in selected cases (SLCG 2.5.3).
Stage IIIB/unresectable IIIA: concurrent chemoradiotherapy then further therapy (SLCG 2.6.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Stage IV
actions: EGFR mutation: EGFR TKI first line; T790M at progression: osimertinib (SLCG 2.7.1.4.1).
Other systemic therapy by histology, driver and PD-L1 per oncology protocol.

learningObjectives: Diagnose, stage and plan treatment for lung cancer.

keyPoints: Urgent CXR or referral by NG12 criteria.
CT then PET-CT for curative candidates.
Surgery for early stage; SBRT if inoperable.
TKI first line for EGFR-mutant disease.
pitfalls: Treating presumed TB or pneumonia without follow-up imaging.
Starting chemotherapy before EGFR results when awaited soon.

patientEducation: Stop smoking (including shisha) at any stage.
mdtReferrals: Lung cancer MDT; palliative care; smoking cessation.
dischargeCriteria: Written plan, named key worker, palliative care contact where needed.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Stage I–III: review every 3 months for 2 years, then 6-monthly for 3 years, then yearly; CT chest every 6 months for 2 years then yearly for 3 years. Stage IV: every 2–3 months (SLCG 2.8).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 40 or over with 2+ symptoms, or ever-smoker with 1
50–80, 20 pack-years, current or quit within 15 years — annual low-dose CT
Nodes 10 mm or more short axis

medicationPlan.note: Systemic anticancer therapy (platinum doublets, tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immunotherapy) is prescribed by oncology under local protocols; the Saudi 2017 guideline names agents but not doses, so no doses are reproduced here.
